<reason>CON won a competitive debate by attacking the motion as a package: a coverage mandate removes the walk-away that makes value-based prices real, while in-year weight/glucose contracts, a duopoly-plus-exceptions formulary, and high discontinuation mean plans likely pay a large certain drug bill and still face later complications. PRO’s best line—walking away from the pill is not walking away from the bill—was memorable but never neutralized dual billing or the scale difference from insulin/biologics. PRO kept a live equity claim about cash-pay rationing, yet CON fairly recast the choice as targeted coverage that can still say no versus a captive buyer, which matches the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s pressure fork on “clinically indicated” vs formulary steering, then the closing flip that the mandate staples a second invoice rather than replacing complications.</best_rebuttal>
